George Borrow, Lavengro, edited by William Ireland Knapp.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/george-borrow/lavengro

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- George Borrow, the author and annotator, died 1881 (Wikidata Q2137717, P570 1881-07-26).
- William Ireland Knapp, the editor and annotator, died 1908 (Wikidata Q3753252, P570 1908-12-05).

First publication of the text used: 1851, Lavengro by George Borrow. The colophon's 1857 date is for The Romany Rye, which is not part of this edition. (SE colophon: 'Lavengro and The Romany Rye were published in 1851 and 1857 respectively by George Borrow.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1851, before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier (George Borrow, the author, died 1881; William Ireland Knapp, the editor, died 1908), so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The country of first publication does not matter.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
